{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793144397663,"sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_011Y3bPeHHBmPae3MnLEozAC","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/nbody/nbody.cpp","content":"// Hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA N-body benchmark.\n//\n// Decomposition:\n//   - MPI: bodies are block-partitioned across ranks. Each rank owns the\n//     velocities and positions of its block and computes forces for it.\n//     Positions are replicated on every rank with MPI_Allgatherv once per step.\n//   - CUDA: each rank drives one GPU (selected by node-local rank). The force\n//     kernel is tiled through shared memory; every body accumulates the\n//     contributions of all other bodies in the same j-order as the serial code,\n//     so results are independent of the number of ranks.\n//   - OpenMP: host-side O(N^2) potential-energy evaluation used by validation.\n//\n// Semantics are preserved: the same integrator, the same per-body summation\n// order, and the same output format as the original serial program.\n\n#ifndef _OPENMP\n#error \"OpenMP is required\"\n#endif\n\n#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\nconstexpr double SOFTENING = 1e-9;\nconstexpr double DT = 0.01;\nconstexpr int BLOCK = 256;\n\nstruct Vec3 {\n    double x, y, z;\n    constexpr Vec3(const double x = 0, const double y = 0, const double z = 0) noexcept : x(x), y(y), z(z) {}\n};\n\nstruct Body {\n    Vec3 pos;\n    Vec3 vel;\n};\n\nstatic_assert(sizeof(Vec3) == 3 * sizeof(double), \"Vec3 must be tightly packed\");\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                                              \\\n    do {                                                                                              \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                                    \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                                    \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, cudaGetErrorString(err_)); \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                                             \\\n        }                                                                                             \\\n    } while (0)\n\nvoid randomizeBodies(std::vector<Body>& bodies, unsigned int seed = 42) {\n    for (auto& body : bodies) {\n        body.pos.x = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.pos.y = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.pos.z = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.x = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.y = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n        body.vel.z = 2.0 * (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 1.0;\n    }\n}\n\n// Force computation for the locally owned bodies [first, first + count).\n// Each thread owns one body and loops over all n bodies in increasing j order,\n// exactly as the serial reference does. Tiles of positions are staged in shared\n// memory; the tile loop keeps the j-order intact.\n// Forces are computed from the positions at the start of the step; positions are\n// only modified by integrateKernel, which runs as a separate launch.\n__global__ void computeForcesKernel(const Vec3* __restrict__ pos, Vec3* __restrict__ vel,\n                                    int n, int first, int count) {\n    __shared__ double sx[BLOCK], sy[BLOCK], sz[BLOCK];\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int li = blockIdx.x * BLOCK + tid;  // local index into owned range\n    const bool active = li < count;\n\n    double pix = 0.0, piy = 0.0, piz = 0.0;\n    if (active) {\n        const Vec3 p = pos[first + li];\n        pix = p.x;\n        piy = p.y;\n        piz = p.z;\n    }\n\n    double Fx = 0.0, Fy = 0.0, Fz = 0.0;\n\n    for (int t = 0; t < n; t += BLOCK) {\n        const int j = t + tid;\n        if (j < n) {\n            const Vec3 p = pos[j];\n            sx[tid] = p.x;\n            sy[tid] = p.y;\n            sz[tid] = p.z;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (active) {\n            const int lim = (n - t < BLOCK) ? (n - t) : BLOCK;\n            for (int k = 0; k < lim; ++k) {\n                const double dx = sx[k] - pix;\n                const double dy = sy[k] - piy;\n                const double dz = sz[k] - piz;\n                const double distSqr = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + SOFTENING;\n                const double invDist = 1.0 / sqrt(distSqr);\n                const double invDist3 = invDist * invDist * invDist;\n\n                Fx += dx * invDist3;\n                Fy += dy * invDist3;\n                Fz += dz * invDist3;\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (active) {\n        vel[li].x += DT * Fx;\n        vel[li].y += DT * Fy;\n        vel[li].z += DT * Fz;\n    }\n}\n\n// Position update for the locally owned bodies.\n__global__ void integrateKernel(Vec3* __restrict__ pos, const Vec3* __restrict__ vel, int first, int count) {\n    const int li = blockIdx.x * BLOCK + threadIdx.x;\n    if (li < count) {\n        const Vec3 v = vel[li];\n        Vec3& p = pos[first + li];\n        p.x += v.x * DT;\n        p.y += v.y * DT;\n        p.z += v.z * DT;\n    }\n}\n\n// Kinetic energy (assuming unit mass), host side.\ndouble computeKineticEnergy(const std::vector<Vec3>& vel) {\n    double energy = 0.0;\n    for (const auto& v : vel) {\n        energy += 0.5 * (v.x * v.x + v.y * v.y + v.z * v.z);\n    }\n    return energy;\n}\n\n// Per-row potential sums for owned bodies: rows[li] = sum over j > i of 1/dist(i, j).\n// Each row is accumulated in fixed j-order, so the result is independent of the\n// OpenMP thread count.\nvoid computePotentialRows(const std::vector<Vec3>& pos, int first, std::vector<double>& rows) {\n    const int n = static_cast<int>(pos.size());\n    const int count = static_cast<int>(rows.size());\n\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 8)\n    for (int li = 0; li < count; ++li) {\n        const int i = first + li;\n        double s = 0.0;\n        for (int j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            const double dx = pos[j].x - pos[i].x;\n            const double dy = pos[j].y - pos[i].y;\n            const double dz = pos[j].z - pos[i].z;\n            const double dist = std::sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz + SOFTENING);\n            s += 1.0 / dist;\n        }\n        rows[li] = s;\n    }\n}\n\n// Validate that simulation produces finite, reasonable values\nbool validateSimulation(const std::vector<Body>& bodies) {\n    for (const auto& body : bodies) {\n        // Check for NaN or Inf values\n        if (!std::isfinite(body.pos.x) || !std::isfinite(body.pos.y) || !std::isfinite(body.pos.z) ||\n            !std::isfinite(body.vel.x) || !std::isfinite(body.vel.y) || !std::isfinite(body.vel.z)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value in body state\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n\n        // Check for extreme values (bodies shouldn't fly off to infinity)\n        const double maxPos = 1e6;\n        const double maxVel = 1e6;\n        if (std::abs(body.pos.x) > maxPos || std::abs(body.pos.y) > maxPos || std::abs(body.pos.z) > maxPos) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: body position exceeds reasonable bounds\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n        if (std::abs(body.vel.x) > maxVel || std::abs(body.vel.y) > maxVel || std::abs(body.vel.z) > maxVel) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: body velocity exceeds reasonable bounds\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of bodies (default: 1024)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -s <num>     Number of simulation steps (default: 10)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation (checks energy conservation)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nstatic int runSimulation(int argc, char** argv, int rank, int size) {\n    int numBodies = 1024;\n    int numSteps = 10;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numBodies = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-s\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numSteps = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (rank == 0) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (numBodies < 0) {\n        if (rank == 0) printf(\"Invalid number of bodies: %d\\n\", numBodies);\n        return 1;\n    }\n\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"N-Body Simulation\\n\");\n        printf(\"Number of bodies: %d\\n\", numBodies);\n        printf(\"Number of steps: %d\\n\", numSteps);\n        printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    }\n\n    // Bind each rank to a GPU based on its node-local rank\n    MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n\n    int devCount = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&devCount));\n    if (devCount == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA devices available on rank %d\\n\", rank);\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(localRank % devCount));\n\n    const int n = numBodies;\n\n    // Initial state (identical on every rank: same seed)\n    std::vector<Body> bodies(n);\n    randomizeBodies(bodies);\n    std::vector<Vec3> h_pos(n), h_vel(n);\n    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        h_pos[i] = bodies[i].pos;\n        h_vel[i] = bodies[i].vel;\n    }\n    std::vector<Body>().swap(bodies);\n\n    // Block partition of bodies across ranks\n    std::vector<int> counts(size), displs(size), cnt3(size), dsp3(size);\n    for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n        counts[r] = n / size + (r < n % size ? 1 : 0);\n        displs[r] = (r == 0) ? 0 : displs[r - 1] + counts[r - 1];\n        cnt3[r] = counts[r] * 3;\n        dsp3[r] = displs[r] * 3;\n    }\n    const int first = displs[rank];\n    const int count = counts[rank];\n\n    // Device allocations (outside the timed region)\n    Vec3* d_pos = nullptr;\n    Vec3* d_vel = nullptr;\n    if (n > 0) CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_pos, n * sizeof(Vec3)));\n    if (count > 0) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_vel, count * sizeof(Vec3)));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d_vel, h_vel.data() + first, count * sizeof(Vec3), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    }\n    const int gridBlocks = (count + BLOCK - 1) / BLOCK;\n\n    // Run simulation\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    for (int step = 0; step < numSteps; ++step) {\n        if (n > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(d_pos, h_pos.data(), n * sizeof(Vec3), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n        }\n        if (count > 0) {\n            computeForcesKernel<<<gridBlocks, BLOCK>>>(d_pos, d_vel, n, first, count);\n            integrateKernel<<<gridBlocks, BLOCK>>>(d_pos, d_vel, first, count);\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(h_pos.data() + first, d_pos + first, count * sizeof(Vec3),\n                                  cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        }\n        // Replicate updated positions on all ranks for the next step\n        MPI_Allgatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, MPI_DATATYPE_NULL, reinterpret_cast<double*>(h_pos.data()),\n                       cnt3.data(), dsp3.data(), MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    }\n\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    const long long localMs = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start).count();\n    long long maxMs = 0;\n    MPI_Reduce(&localMs, &maxMs, 1, MPI_LONG_LONG, MPI_MAX, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n    if (rank == 0) printf(\"Simulation time: %lld ms\\n\", maxMs);\n\n    // Gather final velocities when needed for output or validation\n    const bool needVel = printResults || validate;\n    if (needVel) {\n        if (count > 0) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(h_vel.data() + first, d_vel, count * sizeof(Vec3), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n        }\n        MPI_Allgatherv(MPI_IN_PLACE, 0, MPI_DATATYPE_NULL, reinterpret_cast<double*>(h_vel.data()),\n                       cnt3.data(), dsp3.data(), MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    }\n\n    int rc = 0;\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults && rank == 0) {\n        // Serialize body positions and velocities for hashing\n        std::vector<double> bodyData;\n        bodyData.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(n) * 6);\n        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n            bodyData.push_back(h_pos[i].x);\n            bodyData.push_back(h_pos[i].y);\n            bodyData.push_back(h_pos[i].z);\n            bodyData.push_back(h_vel[i].x);\n            bodyData.push_back(h_vel[i].y);\n            bodyData.push_back(h_vel[i].z);\n        }\n        print_results(bodyData, \"Bodies\");\n    }\n\n    // Validation: check that simulation produces finite, reasonable values\n    if (validate) {\n        // Potential energy: distributed over owned rows, reduced to rank 0\n        std::vector<double> rows(count);\n        computePotentialRows(h_pos, first, rows);\n        double localPot = 0.0;\n        for (double r : rows) localPot += r;\n        double potential = 0.0;\n        MPI_Reduce(&localPot, &potential, 1, MPI_DOUBLE, MPI_SUM, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n\n        if (rank == 0) {\n            printf(\"Validating simulation results...\\n\");\n\n            std::vector<Body> finalBodies(n);\n            for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n                finalBodies[i].pos = h_pos[i];\n                finalBodies[i].vel = h_vel[i];\n            }\n\n            if (validateSimulation(finalBodies)) {\n                const double finalEnergy = computeKineticEnergy(h_vel) - potential;\n                printf(\"Final energy: %.6f\\n\", finalEnergy);\n                printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            } else {\n                printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n                rc = 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (d_pos) CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d_pos));\n    if (d_vel) CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d_vel));\n\n    return rc;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    int provided = 0;\n    MPI_Init_thread(&argc, &argv, MPI_THREAD_FUNNELED, &provided);\n\n    int rank = 0, size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n\n    const int rc {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793144401951,"sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_017DX1x3BMTfkQiSf18Prk6o","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/nbody/CMakeLists.txt","content":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(nbody_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Target the GPUs present on the build machine unless overridden\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native)\nendif()\n\nfind_package(MPI REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(OpenMP REQUIRED COMPONENTS CXX)\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# The single source is compiled as CUDA so that the kernels live alongside the host code\nadd_executable(nbody nbody.cpp)\nset_source_files_properties(nbody.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\n# Optimization and warning flags (host flags forwarded through nvcc)\ntarget_compile_options(nbody PRIVATE\n    -O3\n    -Xcompiler=-march=native\n    -Xcompiler=-Wall\n    -Xcompiler=-Wextra\n    -Xcompiler=-fopenmp\n)\n\ntarget_link_libraries(nbody PRIVATE\n    MPI::MPI_CXX\n    OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX\n    CUDA::cudart\n    m\n)\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/nbody/CMakeLists.txt","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/nbody_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r5/nbody/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1793144401906,"end":1793144401917}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17fbc2b44001hAODQL9bGWqKvk","sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","messageID":"msg_17fbc1f530014WaEp82T5wmwT4"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793144479867,"sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","part":{"id":"prt_17fbd4312001fxLZ8oPSLzQAKa","messageID":"msg_17fbd3cfe0014Jrs56tbO6mTWg","sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","type":"reasoning","text":"I notice the hash changes depending on compiler flags — the plain g++ default build (gnu++17) produced a different hash than explicit -std=gnu++20 builds, which suggests the language standard default is the real variable here, not the fp-contract setting.\n\nSince CMake's CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20 with extensions ON actually compiles as gnu++20, that's the correct baseline to compare against — not the plain default build I used earlier. Checking the outputs in sequence, the new program compiled with -fmad=false matches that gnu++20 baseline exactly, both in hash and final energy value, confirming the match is tied to the CUDA FMA setting rather than fp-contract.\n\nNow I'm weighing whether to keep -fmad=false in the final build, since FMA gives marginal speed gains here but the kernel's bottleneck is sqrt and division anyway, so matching the original's exact numerical output seems worth more than that small performance edge.\n\nI'll update the CMake config to add -fmad=false for CUDA, then rebuild the original reference through CMake too so the comparison is apples-to-apples, and check whether the resulting energy value now matches to six decimal digits.\n\n","time":{"start":1793144472338,"end":1793144479820},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793145785289,"sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","part":{"id":"prt_17fd12132001cKCgKKyDsPTBF1","messageID":"msg_17fd11b930019ygF4Au82ygqQV","sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm seeing odd scaling results: 60x speedup over serial at n=16384, but going from 1 to 4 ranks shows no improvement even though compute should roughly quadruple in throughput. That's suspicious since all processes seem to be sharing the same node's 4 GPUs, so I need to figure out why np=4 isn't actually distributing work faster.\n\nTheoretical math suggests each GPU step should take ~12ms for 120ms total across 10 steps, but we're seeing 335ms — likely a low occupancy issue, since with only 4096 particles per rank split across 4 GPUs, the kernel launches too few blocks (around 16) to fully utilize the 82 SMs, meaning each GPU's work doesn't scale down proportionally with fewer threads per rank.\n\nThe real bottleneck seems to be dependency-chain latency within each thread's accumulator loop, so with fewer threads per GPU, time doesn't shrink since each thread still runs the same number of sequential iterations. One fix is giving each thread multiple independent bodies to process, increasing instruction-level parallelism without touching the summation order or exactness.\n\nEstimating throughput: for np=1 with 16384² interactions per step at ~33.5ms/step, that works out to roughly 200 GFLOPS of FP64 — about a third of the RTX 3090's peak — which is plausible given the expensive sqrt/div operations per interaction. This suggests the single-GPU case is already fairly close to throughput-bound rather than purely latency-bound.\n\nFor np=4, with each GPU handling a quarter of the interactions, I'd expect roughly 4x speedup to ~8ms/step, but the observed time is still ~34ms/step — meaning parallelism isn't actually happening. I suspect all four ranks might be hitting the same GPU despite the local-rank assignment logic, so I want to verify device assignment and monitor nvidia-smi during the np=4 run to confirm whether all four GPUs are actually being utilized concurrently.\n\n","time":{"start":1793145774386,"end":1793145785228},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793145838466,"sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","part":{"id":"prt_17fd1f2fe00186BhWrcTkntJlV","messageID":"msg_17fd1ed9d001AtZv5YeHk3qvPx","sessionID":"ses_e804630f7ffeQ6EtZPrn7MzvMH","type":"reasoning","text":"The nvidia-smi idle reading at 2s likely just means the run finished quickly. Computing per-step timings: np=4 gives about 126-134ms/step while np=1 gives around 485ms/step, which works out to roughly 3.6x scaling across 4 GPUs — confirming the parallelism is genuinely effective.\n\nBut for the 16384 case, both np=1 and np=4 land at the same ~33ms/step, which seems odd given the GPUs have far more capacity than needed. With only 4096-16384 threads involved, occupancy is way under the SM capacity (maybe 10%), so this looks like a latency-bound regime rather than throughput-bound — each thread runs a long dependent chain of FP64 operations, and with so few warps per SM, that latency can't be hidden regardless of how many GPUs are used.\n\nOne possible fix is increasing instruction-level parallelism by having each thread handle multiple independent bodies (sharing tile loads), creating several independent dependency chains per thread. But I'm now second-guessing whether this actually increases the total number of concurrent chains relative to GPU capacity, since the bottleneck seems to be total chains versus available FP64 units across SMs, not just chains per thread.\n\nI recognize that splitting j across threads would change summation order and break bitwise determinism, so it's off the table unless I accept that tradeoff. I'll just note the scalability limit for small N as an inherent cost of maintaining bitwise-exact ordering, and accept the 3.6x speedup at large N as a reasonable result.\n\nNow I'm doing a final cleanup pass: checking the MPI communication and host-device transfers are fine, verifying GPU oversubscription handling when ranks exceed GPUs, and deciding to drop the unused omp.h include since the OpenMP macro check still works without it. Then I'll do one last review of the complete file before finishing.\n\n","time":{"start":1793145828094,"end":1793145838404},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
